text:
Aisha: Heads-up 1 quick plan needed: we're moving from ad-hoc pilots to a small recurring slate (rolling 6-8 partners). Need selection, rollout cadence, and simple SLA for each cohort. Thoughts?
Sam: +1. want a lightweight rubric so we can score quickly and repeatably. Recommend: impact (0-5), infra-fit (0-3), data-readiness (0-2), legal friction (0-2). Top N each month.
Tara: Outreach messaging should focus on expectations: time commitment, data upload needs, and what partners get (tuning, analytics, 1 post-pilot workshop). Keep it short.
Neil: From ML: define required artifacts from partners: 5 canonical prompts + expected output, 1 TPS target, and example error cases. We need this before we deploy them to dedicated routes.
Josh: Ops: we can run a rolling window of two new partners every 2 weeks. That keeps KV/batching steady. Will publish a shared capacity calendar.
Priya: Legal: standardize a brief MOU for pilot terms (4 weeks), include anonymization permission, KMS confirmation, data retention period (default 30 days), and clause for PHI denial unless approved.
Zoe: CS perspective: require a named product contact and a technical contact. Also ask for an internal success metric they care about so we can show ROI.
Aisha: Good. Let's make the SLA minimal: 99% availability on partner routes (within normal infra constraints), per-partner dashboard updates weekly, and 2 engineering hours/week included for tuning. Anything else?
Sam: Add an explicit rollback policy: if automated quality regressions >6% on canonical prompts or error rate >1.5% sustained 12h -> pause and investigate.
Neil: Agree. Also need a mid-pilot check at week 2 to decide on more aggressive tuning vs rollback.
Tara: For recruitment, can we include a "fast-track" checkbox for partners willing to be public case studies? We'll offer a stretch package (extra 4 eng hours) if they commit.
Priya: Case-study consent needs a separate opt-in but we can include a default anonymization allowance. Legal will draft both options.
Josh: Technical ops: I'll create per-partner tokens with cost caps and alerts. Also add a soft throttling knob we can flip if load spikes.
Aisha: Who owns scoring and outreach? Sam do scoring, Tara do outreach + email templates, Josh capacity calendar + tokens, Neil eval dashboard + mid-pilot, Priya legal MOU, Zoe CS onboarding + success metric capture. I'll assemble final playbook and kickoff template.
CS-bot: (automated) pilot template: https://redwood.example/templates/rolling-pilot-playbook
Sam: Proposal for quick rubric scoring sheet: Google sheet with formulas, normalized to 10 points. I'll share after lunch.
Tara: Outreach one-liner draft: "Join a rolling 4-week pilot to tune Redwood inference for your workload. Includes prioritized tuning, weekly metrics, and a post-pilot outcomes workshop."
Zoe: Onboarding checklist for CS: 1) confirm contacts, 2) collect prompts & baselines, 3) calendar kickoff, 4) confirm KMS & data retention, 5) set success metric. Keep it under 6 steps.
Neil: Eval mechanics: automated diffs (token-level) + human review for 10 random samples/week. Need to store baseline outputs in S3 with access controls.
Priya: Legal asks that we provide a short privacy summary for partners to share internally; I'll add that. Also we want an opt-out for anonymized example reuse in public evals.
Aisha: Decision flow: we'll pick the first rolling cohort by next Tue. Sam, share scores Mon noon; Tara start outreach Tue afternoon. If no objections here, I'll lock this plan.
Josh: No infra objections. Calendar will be live by EOD today.
Tara: Comm's happy. I'll prep two email variants (case-study / non-case-study).
Neil: ML ok. Will start dashboard skeleton.
Priya: Legal ok; drafting MOU.
Zoe: CS ok. I'll prep onboarding stub doc.
Aisha: Great. Final note 1 vendors or customers that need private deployment testing get a special flag and go into "private track" (separate SLA). We'll handle that in a follow-up thread.
Sam: Noted.
Aisha: Thanks team — will post the scoring sheet link when available and tag for approvals. :thumbsup:
